chunks: And they say: 'Whatever is in the wombs of these cattle is exclusively for our men and forbidden to our women; but if it is still-born, then they are partners in it.' God will punish them for their assertion. Indeed, He is All-Wise, All-Knowing.
ai.seo_question: What was the pre-Islamic Arab custom regarding the distribution of animal offspring and parts?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse critiques the Jahiliyyah practice of 'tabi'ah' (dedicating specific animal parts), where men claimed exclusive rights to certain cuts while forbidding them to women, yet shared still-born offspring. It underscores the arbitrariness of their man-made prohibitions compared to divine law, serving as a precursor to the detailed rulings on animal sacrifices in Islamic jurisprudence.
